instruction: Correct the Snake game's food initialization so that its spawning position is properly grid-aligned, as implemented in the respawn function.

metadata.explanation: This task requires fixing the food.py initialization bug where Food.__init__ doesn't align food position to the grid (uses random.randint(0, WIDTH-SNAKE_SIZE) directly) while respawn() properly aligns to grid (multiplies by SNAKE_SIZE). The fix is to make __init__ use the same grid-aligned logic as respawn(). The evaluator runs a pathfinding test where the snake moves toward food - if positions are grid-aligned, the snake will reach the food; if not, it will never reach it.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is semantically correct: downloads Snake game files and runs a pathfinding test where the snake moves toward food using greedy navigation
Test logic is clever and valid: if food is grid-aligned (bug fixed), snake will reach food; if not grid-aligned (bug present), snake will never reach it due to grid-based movement
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter: uses 'expected.get("passed", True)' to directly access the rules dict (correct pattern for type="rule")
Expected value is correct: expects passed=true when the grid alignment bug is fixed
Coverage is complete: the pathfinding test directly verifies the core requirement (grid alignment) by testing if snake can reach food
Practical feasibility: getter can download files, import modules, and run test; 1000 iteration limit is reasonable for this deterministic test
